claims.claim: Clement of Rome, also known as Pope Clement I, was the Bishop of Rome in the late first century and is considered to be the first of the Apostolic Fathers of the Church.
The First Epistle of Clement is internally anonymous but is attributed to Clement I, the fourth bishop of Rome, which most scholars hold to be true.
The most common time given for the epistle's composition is at the end of the reign of Domitian, around AD 96.
The letter was written by the Church of God which sojourns in Rome to the Church of God which sojourns in Corinth.
The letter was occasioned by a dispute in Corinth, which had led to the removal from office of several presbyters.
The author called on the congregation to repent, to restore the presbyters to their position, and to obey their superiors.
In Corinth, the letter was read aloud from time to time, and this practice spread to other churches.
Christians translated the letter from the original Greek into Latin, Syriac, and other languages.
The work was lost for centuries, but since the 1600s various copies or fragments have been found and studied.
